#2576. Prisco's NFL Week 11 Power Rankings: Patrick Mahomes returns to MVP form, which makes Chiefs scary

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

All we heard for much of this season was that the Kansas City Chiefs had taken on a new offensive persona. They were now a running team with Kenneth Walker.

Yes, they have leaned on the running game for the early part of the season, in large part because of a lack of quality receivers, the addition of Walker and quarterback Patrick Mahomes recovering from a torn ACL in 2025. But Sunday's blowout victory over the Atlanta Falcons reminded us that this team will go only as far as the right arm of Mahomes, who looked all the way back from the ACL injury Sunday and overcame an elbow injury suffered last week.

With Walker missing the Falcons game because of a groin injury, all Mahomes did was throw for 348 yards and five touchdowns to remind the doubters that he is much more than a game manager who just turns and hands the ball off.

Walker has been mentioned as an MVP candidate. Reminder: He isn't even the MVP on his own team. Mahomes is that.

The addition of receiver Josh Downs at the trade deadline helps give Mahomes more weapons. Downs had a touchdown Sunday, as did rookie speedster Cyrus Allen, who may be on the verge of breaking out.

The backfield was also in good hands with rookie running back Emmett Johnson, who scored two touchdowns and accounted for 171 total yards, rushing for 101. He was able to replace Walker easily, but that injury largely forced the Chiefs to turn back to Mahomes of old.

The 7-2 Chiefs are still sixth in my Power Rankings this week, but as that passing game gets back to what we've come to see in other years from Mahomes, they will be a real Super Bowl threat.

When Walker comes back, they can run it with anybody. With Mahomes under center, they can throw it with anybody -- especially with the receiver group improving.

The defense is ranked third in scoring, giving up just 17.3 points per game. They are eighth in total defense and tied for sixth in yards allowed per play.

Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has this young group playing good defense.

The Chiefs are back. Mostly, though, Mahomes is back, which is why they are a real threat in the AFC to go to the Super Bowl. You want to go to Arrowhead to play them in the playoffs with that guy? Didn't think so.

As for the bottom of the rankings, the Los Angeles Chargers have moved on up. Not much, but they are out of the cellar after beating the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night. The Tennessee Titans are now the bottom dwellers of my rankings.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2574. Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The big prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. We've seen and will continue to see predictions that he's going to land a deal of around 8-10 years and topping $400 million. The knee-jerk reaction to such prognostications in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

Let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.

Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

Since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

The recent track record here says this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

There isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the big-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

We'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a new procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

Skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

Again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. If he signs an eight-year deal, it'll run through his age-37 season.

For those so worried about the long-term finances of the team owner who ends up signing Skubal, are you sure you're really worried that he won't be productive through five, six, seven or even all eight years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

Gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

Justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

David Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

Corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

Zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

Max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

We can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

By this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:

Are you sure a 10-year, $400 million deal for this guy would be a "risk?"

I think we could argue that it would be a bargain.

#2573. Caleb Wilson reportedly out 4-6 weeks with broken hand, taking away the only reason to watch the Bulls

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The NBA injury train is showing no signs of slowing down as Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson will undergo surgery for a fractured right hand and miss four to six weeks of action, according to ESPN.

Wilson, the No. 4 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, was injured in Wednesday night's loss to the Spurs. He was off to a great start for the otherwise struggling Bulls, who are now 1-9. He's an electric watch as a 6-foot-9, gliding athlete with every tool in the kit. He's averaging 18.9 points, 6.2 boards and nearly two steals a night so far. Before the injury, Wilson was listed at 15-1 to win Rookie of the Year, but within minutes of the news of his injury surfacing, those odds fell to 40-1 at FanDuel.

Before the injury, those were the fifth-best odds, which in most classes might not sound like a player having as good a start as Wilson, but this is an absolutely stacked rookie class with Yaxel Lendeborg being an actual All-Star candidate, Darius Acuff Jr. averaging over 26 points per game, Darryn Peterson averaging over 23 points in his last four and Cameron Boozer stuffing the stat sheet at 15.9 points, 9.8 rebounds and 5.5 assists a night for a Grizzlies team on the rise.

Wilson is the future in Chicago, and in the long term, that's all that matters. They almost have to look to trade Norman Powell before the deadline, and Nic Claxton should join him on the way out. Powell's deal is particularly priced to be moved as next year's $22.5 million is a team option. That's a good number for a player of Powell's worth but could also be an expiring deal for a team looking to use him for a championship push and then reassess over the summer with no long-term commitment.

However that plays out, the next month and change is going to be even more brutal for Bulls fans than the first three weeks of the season have been now that Wilson, like so many other of the league's most exciting players, is headed for street clothes.

This news of Wilson's injury comes on the same day that the Warriors listed Stephen Curry out for at least the next two weeks with an oblique tear. From Anthony Edwards to Jalen Williams, Tyrese Haliburton, Jaren Jackson Jr., Ja Morant, Kawhi Leonard, Cason Wallace, Paolo Banchero, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Duren, Curry and beyond, this is a massive issue that the NBA, in some capacity, needs to take meaningful steps toward at least attempting to resolve.

Fans are paying way too much money not to watch the best players, and for the Bulls, Wilson was the main attraction for a team that will struggle to win games. Outside of diehards who are going to tune in no matter what, absolutely no casual fan has an interest in watching Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis on a 1-9 team. That's the harsh truth.

#2572. Ranking the 50 QBs who have started an NFL game in 2026: From cellar-dwellers to gold standard

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

So far, quarterback injuries and a revolving door of quarterbacks represent defining aspects of the 2026 NFL season. That number reached 50 quarterbacks in Week 10, which would be a staggering amount for an entire season.

So where do they all stack up? The rankings were broken down into 10 tiers, with three quarterbacks getting their own tier.

Nobody wants to be here, but their performances have nonetheless left them in the basement. Of all the quarterbacks in this group, Herbert is the most notable given all the success he experienced during his first six seasons in Los Angeles.

Herbert hasn't been good, but it's not all on him. His supporting cast hasn't carried its weight, and the Chargers' coaching staff (especially Jim Harbaugh and OC Mike McDaniel) aren't on the same page.

If there's a silver lining for Herbert, it's that Peyton Manning had a similar season at a similar point in his career. Manning bounced back all the way to the Hall of Fame. We'll see how Herbert responds to this adversity.

Mendoza gets his own tier for two reasons: he's had just one start, and that start was a mixed bag. Overall, it was a promising debut for the No. 1 overall pick.

Facing Seattle's "Dark Side" defense, Mendoza went 11 of 13 in the first half and scored the only touchdown before intermission on a 10-yard run. Mendoza was less effective in the second half as Seattle ratcheted up the pressure. He finished with 143 yards on 17 of 29 passing in a 21-13 loss.

Each of these backups experienced various levels of success.

McCarthy, traded from the Vikings to address New York's injury situation, is getting another chance (albeit temporary) to be an NFL starting quarterback. As was the case in Minnesota, McCarthy has shown signs of being a solid player in New York, but he still needs to work on his consistency, among other things.

Take last week, for example. McCarthy threw for 293 yards and a touchdown and made some plays with his feet, but he also threw an ugly interception that sealed New York's loss to Washington.

Daniels, the only rookie in this group, led the Buccaneers to their first win of the season, an upset in Dallas back in Week 5. A week later, he took Tampa Bay to overtime in an eventual loss to the Steelers.

Mayfield was included here because his performance this season is most in line with this tier. He threw just 14 combined passes in his two wins as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He made odd history in Week 8 by becoming the first quarterback since 1974 to win a start without completing a single pass.

These quarterbacks have had moments of success this season, but those moments have often been overshadowed by shortcomings.

Hurts is dealing with something much bigger than football. He's been away from the team since blood clots were discovered following the Eagles' Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London. The Eagles said at the time that Hurts' prognosis is "very good" and that he is expected to make a full recovery.

Murray is listed as a starter here, but there's a very good chance that, barring injury, he has made his final start for the Vikings. Minnesota's production with him under center just wasn't up to snuff.

22. Geno Smith, Jets     21. Drake Maye, Patriots

18. Aaron Rodgers, Steelers  17. Bryce Young, Panthers

These guys aren't the first quarterbacks taken in fantasy football drafts, and for good reason: they don't consistently put up numbers. They are, however, above-average quarterbacks who once in a while show flashes of greatness, just not enough to be ranked higher.

Rodgers' production isn't close to what it once was, but he has continued to play good football (especially for a 42-year-old) while helping the Steelers get off to a 6-3 start. A big reason Rodgers hasn't had more success is Pittsburgh's lack of receiving weapons, a need that wasn't addressed at the trade deadline.

Nix had a slow start to the season, which was probably a byproduct of January's season-ending ankle injury. His play has improved in recent weeks, which is certainly good news for a Broncos team with Super Bowl aspirations.

Watson has struggled with his consistency and production from a touchdown standpoint (he hasn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5), but he's been good enough to win six of his nine starts. Each of Cleveland's wins featured game-winning drives led by Watson.

Maye's tumultuous season took a disastrous turn Sunday when he suffered a potentially season-ending ankle injury.

Each backup quarterback that has started a game this season has had various levels of success. None has been better than Lock, who is 3-0 this year as Seattle's starting quarterback. Lock's stellar play (he has had seven touchdowns, no picks, and has completed 73.1% of his passes) has led to rumblings about whether or not he should be the starter in Seattle moving forward.

Stroud has put up good numbers, and he is far from Houston's biggest problem. Houston had seven players miss Sunday's loss to Cleveland due to injury. Their running game has been largely non-existent, and the defense has underperformed all year.

Prescott continues to be one of the league's most prolific passers, but most of his production has come against bad teams or when the Cowboys were trying to catch up, as was the case during Sunday's loss to the 49ers.

Cousins' performance in Sunday's win over the Packers was nothing short of amazing. Just days after being traded from Las Vegas, Cousins threw a pair of scores and completed 67.7% of his passes while leading Minnesota to a 30-10 win. If Cousins keeps this up, the Vikings could very well win the NFL's hardest division, if not the Super Bowl.

Per usual, Daniels has been excellent this season when healthy. Dart was off to a strong start before an injury ended his sophomore season after just two weeks.

Jackson was off to another strong start before a thumb injury derailed his season and the Ravens'. Williams missed three games earlier this season, and while his play has been mostly good, his production has been somewhat lacking (he has just three games with multiple touchdown passes this season). His four-pick performance in Chicago's Week 9 win over Tampa was a tough watch.

Stafford, the league's reigning MVP, has displayed remarkable resilience this season amid the Rams' early losses and injuries to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. He won't win a second MVP this season, but in some ways, Stafford's performance so far this season is just as impressive.

Stafford's predecessor in Los Angeles, Goff continues to play at a high level in Detroit. His success has led to continued success for the Lions, who are once again in the thick of the NFC North race.

Allen, the MVP front-runner for most of the season's first half, doesn't have as many touchdown passes (13) as his peers, but he does have a league-high 11 touchdown runs. He's also the catalyst for the Bills' 8-1 start.

Purdy has been rock solid all year for the 8-1 49ers, but it's fair to wonder whether his strong supporting cast will negatively impact his MVP chances. Regardless, Purdy is playing the best ball of his career and is a big reason why the 49ers are the cream of the NFC crop.

Love skyrocketed up the QB charts over the last six weeks prior to Sunday's setback to the visiting Vikings. Sunday's game exposed the Packers' beat-up offensive line and their lack of a running game without Josh Jacobs. Love is exceptional, but he can only do so much.

Lawrence is a chameleon in that he can conform to whatever the Jaguars need him to be on a weekly basis in order to win. That's led to some gaudy games for Lawrence and other games where he has excelled in a supporting role. That has helped the Jaguars get to 7-2.

Mahomes earned a spot in this tier following his performances over the last three weeks. Outside of the No. 1 quarterback on our list, no quarterback has played better over that span than Mahomes. In the Chiefs' last three games, Mahomes has thrown 10 touchdowns, zero interceptions, completed 70% of his passes and averaged 304 passing yards per game. MVP-type stuff if you ask me.

Already the MVP favorite entering Sunday night's game against the Steelers, Burrow is now the clear front-runner. Against a team that defeated the Bengals back in Week 3, Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns while completing nearly 80% of his passes.

Burrow's performance not only strengthened his MVP case but also put him on a historic trajectory with eight games to play in the 2026 regular season. He is one of only five quarterbacks in NFL history with over 30 total touchdowns through nine games, according to CBS Sports Research. The other four (Tom Brady in 2007, Rodgers in 2011, Peyton Manning in 2013 and Mahomes in 2018) won league MVP:

Burrow is on track to create his own category for quarterback excellence by becoming the first quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing 70% of his passes. If he does that, he will have a strong argument when it comes to having the greatest passing season in league history.

#2570. MLB rumors: Phillies OF on the trading block, Blue Jays eye ex-Yankee, plus Mets, Mariners, Braves, Rays, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas. Though we haven't seen any major moves this offseason, we have seen an uptick in rumors in the past few days and that isn't a coincidence. Put a bunch of reporters and front-office execs in the same area for three or four days and chatter picks up, even if there isn't a ton of actual substance behind it.

Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.

We have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. Phillips ranked No. 34 on our top 50 free agent list.

Phillips, a 32-year-old right-hander, has been a setup man or closer for the Dodgers for the last several seasons. In returning from surgery last season, he appeared in 31 games, pitching to a 3.46 ERA and 1.07 WHIP with 33 strikeouts in 26 innings. The majority of his closing experience came in 2023 when he had 24 saves in 27 chances.

The Braves' closer last season was Raisel Iglesias, but he's a free agent. Holdover Robert Suarez could take over those duties while Phillips, lefty Dylan Lee and youngster Didier Fuentes are also in the late-inning mix.

The Blue Jays went from one of the best offensive teams in 2025 to one of the worst in 2026. They'd love a big bounceback from Vladimir Guerrero Jr., among other positive movements, but they also look for outside help. Might that help come in the form of free agent infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.?

The Jays have met with representatives for Chisholm, reports Sportsnet.

Chisholm, 28, hit .231/.312/.399 last season, but had a huge 2025 and any signing team would be hoping for the 2025 version of Chisholm.

The Jays do have a capable incumbent second baseman in Ernie Clement, but either Clement or Chisholm can be used in the outfield and the Blue Jays certainly need outfield upgrades.

The Phillies have been telling opposing teams that they are not "locked into anything" regarding their current outfield situation, according to The Athletic, so much so that All-Star outfielder Brandon Marsh is available in a trade.

As things stand, with Bryce Harper moving back to first base, the Phillies would have Bryan De La Cruz in right, Justin Crawford in center and Marsh in left, but that all seems pretty fluid as they look to upgrade the ballclub and keep that window of contention open.

Marsh, 28, had a stellar start last season, leading to his first-ever All-Star Game. Through July 1, he hit .319/.352/.530. The rest of the way, however, he slashed .177/.241/.241, dragging him down overall to a 90 OPS+ and 0.4 WAR on the season.

The Mariners have shown interest in free agent left fielder Ian Happ, per MLB Network.

Happ, 32, has spent his entire 10-year MLB career with the Cubs, who drafted him in the first round all the way back in 2015. He was pretty consistent from 2022-25, averaging 3.9 WAR with a .251/.347/.433 (118 OPS+) line and winning four Gold Gloves. Last season, though, he dipped to .218/.326/.412 (103 OPS+) with 2.7 WAR. He still topped 20 home runs for the fifth time in the last six years.

The Mariners have a vacancy in left field with Randy Arozarena having hit free agency and a need to upgrade their offense.

Yesterday's big news was the Yankees' interest in free agent first/third baseman Alec Bohm and The Athletic reports that we can now add the Mets to the list of suitors.

Bohm hit .249/.315/.383 (87 OPS+) with 15 home runs, 88 RBI and -0.2 WAR last season. It might be surprising to see him garnering such interest on the open market, but there isn't much right-handed power out there and Bohm finished last season strong (.318/.402/.453 in his last 42 games). The Mets, meanwhile, are desperate for help at the cold corner after last year's disastrous Jorge Polanco experiment. Jared Young did provide a glimmer of hope at first base before suffering a concussion in September while colliding with a teammate on a play.

Free agent starting pitcher Dustin May has a decent market right now, according to MLB Network, with at least the Cubs, White Sox, Padres and Astros having shown interest in the right-hander.

May, 29, made 31 starts between the Cardinals and Brewers last season, going 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 145 ⅔ innings. He showed flashes of brilliance with the Cardinals and had a stretch from April 10 to June 15 during which he posted a 2.54 ERA in 12 starts, but in the end there was plenty of inconsistency and even bad, forcing him into a bullpen role in the playoffs for the champion Brewers.

Free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers has been extended the qualifying offer from the Twins, meaning he has to decide by net Tuesday whether to accept the one-year, $23.15 million contract or hit free agency. There's nothing that says a team can't re-sign a player after he declines their qualifying offer, of course, and it sounds like that path is possible in this case.

Jeffers will decline the QO and the Twins are interested in reaching a multi-year deal to bring him back, reports the Minnesota Star-Tribune. Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 with 14 home runs for Minnesota in 2026, a standout line for a catcher, though he missed several months with a broken hamate. The Twins do have several catchers in their farm system, including Vahn Lackey, the No. 3 pick in last year's draft, and Eduardo Tait, who headlined the trade return for Jhoan Duran.

Much has been said and will continue to be said about the 2027 free agent class and how it looks relatively weak, especially on the position-player side, where the best players are the likes of Jazz Chisholm Jr., Seiya Suzuki, and the aforementioned Arozarena and Jeffers.

As we know, the Rays love to find avenues where they can exploit market inefficiencies. Their latest move might be to hit the trade market with center fielder Jonny DeLuca in anticipation of moving Victor Mesa Jr. to center, according to The Athletic.

DeLuca, 28, got more playing time than ever before in 2026, appearing in 112 games and getting 370 plate appearances. He hit .266/.300/.429 (101 OPS+) with 11 homers, 50 RBI, 17 steals and 1.7 WAR.

Fresh off a playoff berth despite the lowest payroll in all of baseball at a paltry $75ish million, the Guardians are planning to increase payroll. Or so they say.

"We'll go up," club president Chris Antonetti told The Athletic. "We have to."

The Guardians hosted six playoff games and made some money there, not to mention that they have a bunch of players hitting arbitration and surely they want to spend more to remain competitive. There's an added wrinkle here, too, which would be that the ownership side is really pushing hard for a salary cap when the upcoming CBA expires in a few weeks. With a cap comes a floor and we've seen MLB float proposals with salary floors in the $180 million range, or well more than double what the Guardians had last season.

So, yeah, I'd say the Guardians "have to" increase payroll, one way or another.

#2569. Rockets' Marcus Smart suspended three games for punching Warriors' Charles Bassey during in-game scuffle

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The NBA has suspended Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart for three games for "throwing a punch that made contact with the face" of Golden State Warriors big man Charles Bassey, the league announced on Thursday.

The incident came late in the third quarter of Wednesday night's game in Houston. After Smart and Bassey got tangled up on the other end of the floor, Smart chased Bassey down and threw a punch at his head area. They were quickly broken up from there, and Smart was eventually ejected from the game with a flagrant-2 foul. Despite his absence, the Rockets went on to win the game, 115-108.

MARCUS SMART PUNCHES CHARLES BASSEY 😳 pic.twitter.com/MUsLlDHCz4

What triggered the incident? "I just talked to [Smart]. He said they got wrapped up, and [Smart]'s elbow that he hurt got bent up," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said after the game. "So, [Smart] said something to him. Bassey said, 'What are you going to do?' And he did it."

Bassey, on the other hand, blamed Smart for what happened. "He's been playing dirty the whole game," the Warriors big man said. "In the first half, I was trying to set a screen and he grabbed my knee. So I mean, he was playing dirty. [On the play in question], I think I was trying to get a rebound and he was grabbing my hand and I was trying to run back on defense. ... And then he got up on me and swung. Obviously that was weak. I think that was, honestly, fake toughness."

Charles Bassey on Marcus Smart throwing a punch at him: “Fake toughness.”“I don’t think he was trying to play. I think he was trying to get himself out of the game.” pic.twitter.com/ZxbgvUDeY9

As for what sort of words were exchanged between Smart and Bassey? "He said something to me," Bassey explained. "He said something like, 'Hey, don't do that.' I said, 'Do what?' It's a grown-man's league."

Smart is no stranger to NBA discipline. He has 12 ejections, nine fines (excluding flopping and technical foul fines) and two suspensions across his 13-year career. Now, the 9-3 Rockets will be without a key guard for the next three games, but fortunately for them, their next three opponents are all below .500: the Utah Jazz, Washington Wizards and Miami Heat.

#2568. Giants' Cam Skattebo says he's done doing backflip celebration after Aidan Hutchinson's injury

EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. (AP) — New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he is done doing his signature backflip celebration after Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson injured his right knee celebrating a sack Sunday against New England and is out for the rest of the season.

"It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters from NJ.com and the New York Post after practice Wednesday. "Mentally, I'm like: 'I'm not doing that. That ain't going to happen to me.'"

Skattebo got into hot water with team officials over the summer when he landed awkwardly doing a backflip. He spent several months rehabbing from surgery to repair a broken right fibula and dislocated ankle.

"The big picture message is you want to take care of yourself," coach John Harbaugh said at the time. "You want to take care of your team. Do everything you can do to be healthy, be back, be right, be good."

Skattebo has rushed for 496 yards and four touchdowns on 116 carries in his second year in the NFL, including two scores last Thursday night against Washington. He lost a fumble in overtime in the first meeting against the Commanders on Oct. 11, which led him to getting only six offensive snaps and zero carries the following week when the Giants played New Orleans.

#2567. NFL Week 11 picks and score predictions: 49ers win Mexico City thriller over Vikings, Bengals stay hot

I have made it 24 years without watching a single episode of "The Bachelor,"  but that streak might soon be coming to an end because an NFL quarterback has been chosen to star in the show.

Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman is this year's bachelor, and the only reason I'm mentioning that is that I'm not quite mentally ready to start talking about Week 11 yet. I just looked at the Week 11 schedule and what the NFL is giving us during the 1 p.m. window might be the worst slate of games ever.

There are seven games in the early window, and none of them will feature two teams with winning records facing off. Let's take a look at this schedule:

I would rather watch old episodes of "The Bachelor" than any of these games. That being said, I might watch the Cowboys game just to see if Jerry Jones fires everyone after his defense gives up 47 points to the Titans.

So will that actually happen? Let's get to the picks and find out.

For the second straight week, we have a team coming off a game in Europe facing a team coming off a bye. Last week, things worked out pretty well for the Bengals, but that feels like an anomaly. This game will mark just the seventh time in NFL history that a team coming off an international game has had to play a team coming off a bye, and uh, I have some bad news for everyone in Detroit: The team coming off the international game has gone 1-5, with the only win coming by a possessed Bengals team in Week 10 that got to host a Sunday night game at home for the first time in three years. There was no way the Bengals were losing.

However, I am worried about the Lions. For one, they just lost Aidan Hutchinson for the season to a torn ACL, and thanks to the injury, there's a 50% chance that Dan Campbell is going to ban his entire team from celebrating anything ever again.

Aidan Hutchinson suffered an injury on this play and went to the locker room.(📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/ysx9NLmNHF

Not only did they just lose their best defensive player, but it gets worse, because they now have to face the top rushing offense in the NFL. The Bucs are averaging 163.9 yards per game on the ground, which is 10 yards more than the next closest team. Tampa Bay has more rushing yards this season than the Bengals and Packers COMBINED.

I do not know if Baker Mayfield (foot) is going to play, but I'm not sure it matters, because the QB in Tampa only has one job and that's to hand the ball off. If Baker can't play, Jalon Daniels will, and if he can't play for some reason, the Bucs could probably just hold a fan raffle for the job.

Bucs: Can you hand the ball off? Fan: Yes. Bucs: OK, the job is yours.

There have only been three games this season where an NFL team has run the ball at least 49 times and the Buccaneers have two of them. With the Buccaneers coming off the bye, that means they're going to be well-rested and it also means that offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has had plenty of time to tear out every page from his playbook that has a passing play on it. The Bucs might run it 71 times on Sunday.

The good news for the Lions is that they've been one of the best teams in the NFL at stopping the run. They're giving up just 90.4 yards per game, which is the fifth-best number in the NFL, but that was with Hutchinson on the field. This week, they obviously won't have him.

The Lions are flying back from Germany; they just lost their best defensive player, and they have to face a Bucs team coming off a bye. Oh, and did I mention that NFL teams are a combined 13-3 coming off their bye this year? Because NFL teams are a combined 13-3 coming off their bye this year. And two of those three losses were by the Titans and Chargers, so I'm not even sure those count.

Not only do the Bucs have the best rushing attack in the NFL, but they also have the best run defense in the league, so this could be a long day for Jahmyr Gibbs. This game comes down to whether you trust Jared Goff to dice up Tampa Bay's defense, and, well, I'm the guy who made Goff my preseason prediction to win MVP this year, so I'm riding with Goff and the Lions here.

If there's any game in Week 11 that feels like a disaster waiting to happen, it's definitely this one. With the Jets and Chargers on the same field, I won't be surprised if the government declares SoFi Stadium a federal disaster area.

There's been no bigger disaster in the NFL this year than the Chargers. They hired Mike McDaniel to fix their offense and he somehow might have made it worse. When McDaniel was in Miami, one reason his offense worked so well is that he had two superstar receivers in Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle. He doesn't have anything near that in L.A., but he does not seem to realize that. McDaniel keeps doing things his own way, and as a result, the Chargers' offense is so bad it's almost painful to watch.

It's getting to the point where I feel like the Chargers' best offensive strategy would be to just not have an offense at all. I have no idea how that would work, but I have to think it would be an upgrade over what they're doing now. This team is averaging UNDER 180 passing yards per game, which shouldn't be possible when you have Justin Herbert as your QB.

Not to be outdone, the Jets have also been a disaster. Here's a quick synopsis of how things have gone for the Jets. Back on Feb. 24, Aaron Glenn said he would call plays on defense because it's one of his superpowers.

"To me, play calling is my superpower"Aaron Glenn on his decision to call plays on defense pic.twitter.com/FvHFYW97pK

As it turns out, though, he might have been wrong, and play-calling might actually be his kryptonite.

Aaron Glenn gave up play calling vs the #Bills — that’s really big of him. Called it his “super power” this offseason. He wants to call the game. To step back and be willing to give it to someone else, for the betterment of the team, isn’t something a lot of coaches are willing… https://t.co/ivYq4cnBca

Aaron Glenn saw Josh Allen coming up on the schedule in Week 10 and said "No thanks, I'm good. You're now in charge of calling play on defense, Brian."

So we have the Jets' broken defense going up against a Chargers offense that can't move the ball on anyone. I said this game feels like a disaster waiting to happen and that disaster might happen after the game. If the Jets lose here, the temperature on Aaron Glenn's hot seat will get so hot that I don't think the Fahrenheit scale can actually measure it. We might have to switch over to Celsius.

The Chargers stunned the Ravens on Monday night by rushing for a season-high 160 yards. Running the ball is literally the only thing the Chargers can do on offense, which might work in their favor here because the Jets can't stop the run.

The Chargers went into Week 10 with ZERO wins, so I feel crazy even thinking this, but this team might actually win two games in a row.

Never in my life did I think I would live long enough to see a Jaguars-Giants game get flexed into the 4:25 p.m. late afternoon slot, but that's exactly what happened here. This game was originally scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET, but the NFL decided to move it to 4:25 p.m. ET, and we're celebrating that fact here at CBS Sports by sending "The NFL Today" crew to MetLife Stadium.

The NFL Today is headed to MetLife! 🔥The show will be LIVE outside the stadium ahead of @Jaguars vs @Giants this Sunday 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Bv2zAZ1htI

If you're going to be at the game, please come dressed as your favorite CBS Sports studio analyst.

The Giants have been a huge surprise this season, and that's mostly thanks to John Harbaugh, who is my early vote for coach of the year. Harbaugh has been forced to start THREE different quarterbacks this season, but he still has the Giants at 5-3-1 and on top of the NFC East.

The biggest surprise is that the Giants have somehow made J.J. McCarthy look good. I was led to believe by the Vikings that McCarthy was a washed-up bust, but apparently they just didn't know how to use him. McCarthy is the chopsticks of NFL quarterbacks. I hate chopsticks because I'm incompetent and don't know how to use them, just like the Vikings didn't know how to use McCarthy. On the other hand, my wife is such an expert with chopsticks that if every utensil on earth disappeared tomorrow and we only had chopsticks left, she would be fine, just like the Giants will be fine with McCarthy running the show.

McCarthy played well enough to win in Week 10 against the Commanders, and the Giants might have won if they had a kicker who could make field goals from the right hash.

All 6 of Dominic Zvada’s missed kicks this season have come from the right hash, including his 33-yard miss last night.The Giants have lined up on the left hash for every extra point, where Zvada is a perfect 16/16. https://t.co/D9YzxVSYyx pic.twitter.com/UHJa8av5EK

Zvada's inability to hit a kick from the right hash is like Zoolander not being able to turn left, except worse.

I watched zoolander today (kind of like idiocracy) and the main character DEREK zoolander. Cannot turn left. Where have i heard of a derek related to the direction left. pic.twitter.com/e8cUEOU8Ct

Although I think the Giants will keep this game close, this will be the first week that the Jaguars finally unveil their new defense. They made three trades before the deadline, acquiring DT Davon Godchaux, DT Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III. The Jags decided to keep Davis and Bates on the bench in Week 10 so they would each get a "bye" week this year. Those two will make their debut on Sunday, and I have a feeling the new-look Jags' defense is going to cause some problems for the Giants.

For the first time in four years, the NFL is playing a game in Mexico City. I went to Mexico City once, and I was totally blown away by the food. I mean, they had a Chili's and Burger King UNDER THE SAME ROOF.

If you're looking for food in Mexico City, I highly recommend this place. Only place I know of where you can get the world's two best restaurants under one roof TOGETHER pic.twitter.com/G58xvmA5DS

Someone needs to make that happen in the United States. Mexico is light years ahead of us when it comes to combining fast food with fast casual dining under one roof.

OK, I need to stop talking about Chili's and start focusing on what could be the best chess match of the 2026 season: Kyle Shanahan vs. Brian Flores.

Through the first 10 weeks, the 49ers have had one of the best offenses in the NFL this year: They rank first in yards per game (399.8) and second in points per game (31.2). No one has really been able to stop them. The 49ers are so good that the Cowboys' defense basically gave up on trying to stop them in Week 10.

As for the Vikings, they have one of the best defenses in the NFL. They've given up the fewest points per game (14) and the second-fewest yards per game (273.3). One big reason they're so successful is that they've gotten really good at destroying the opposing quarterback. The Vikings have racked up 37 sacks this year, which leads the NFL, and Flores loves to blitz on nearly every single play.

The problem with that strategy is that Brock Purdy is basically the one quarterback you do NOT want to blitz.

Leaders in EPA per drop back vs the blitz…DO NOT blitz these guys pic.twitter.com/Vn67jHblTm

Purdy thinks fast and gets rid of the football quickly. It's like he was designed in a lab to beat the blitz, but Flores is almost certainly aware of this, which means we'll probably see him cook up something special for the 49ers quarterback on Sunday. And now that we're talking about cooking, I'm thinking of Chili's again. I might need to take a lunch break.

I actually think the X-factor in this game is going to be the altitude. Mexico City sits at an elevation of nearly 7,400 feet, which is more than 2,000 feet higher than Denver. When you're playing at an altitude this high, it's not easy to get acclimated, which is why the 49ers will be spending the entire week in Colorado Springs, a city that has an altitude of just over 6,000 feet.

#49ers are set to travel to Colorado Springs tonight to begin altitude acclimation. They’ll have a normal practice week before traveling to Mexico City on Saturday to play the Vikings on Sunday night.

On the other hand, the Vikings will be practicing at their normal practice facility, which has an altitude of 945 feet. Advantage, 49ers.

This feels like a game where the altitude starts to get to the Vikings in the second half and that's when the 49ers will take over.

This is the final international game of the 2026 season, and I feel like the NFL should add some spice to the last international game each year by having the government revoke the losing team's passports. I'm not sure if that's legal, but I would definitely watch a reality show that consisted only of NFL players trying to get back home after having their passports revoked in a foreign country. It would be more entertaining than "The Bachelor."

Dan Quinn is probably going to be having nightmares all week and that's because he has to figure out a way to stop Joe Burrow, which is something that no one else has been able figure how to do this year.

At this point, you've probably seen plenty of Burrow highlights this year, but if you're wondering just how dominant he's been, let me break it down for you:

To put his yardage number in perspective, no other QB is even averaging 285 yards per game. He has five more TD passes than the next closest player and his completion percentage is so high that he might actually break the NFL single-season record of 74.4%, which was set by Drew Brees in 2019.

Burrow is playing at an insanely high level, and now, he gets to face a Commanders defense that has given up the most passing yards per game in the NFC this year and second-most in the NFL (244.8). Burrow against this defense would be like inviting Joey Chestnut to your family's Thanksgiving and telling him to eat whatever he wants. You know you're going to get a Hall of Fame performance.

Sam Darnold threw for 379 yards against this Commanders defense. Jameis Winston threw for 326 yards against this defense. J.J. McCarthy threw for 293 yards against this defense. I think what I'm trying to say here is that the NFL might want to invite Norm Van Brocklin's family to this game, because Burrow might take down his all-time single-game passing record of 554 yards.

Although I feel like Burrow is going to have a big game, I think the Commanders' offense could also have some success. This is a home primetime game; Washington will be desperate, and Jayden Daniels has been playing well over the past few weeks.

The last time these two teams played back in 2024, there wasn't a single punt in the game. That might happen again on Monday night because Zac Taylor doesn't sound like a guy who plans on punting this week.

Asked what he didn't like about last night's blowout win against the Steelers, #Bengals coach Zac Taylor said, "We punted."

I'm going to say Burrow continues his MVP campaign by leading the Bengals to a shootout win in Washington.

Texans 24-17 over ColtsBills 30-16 over DolphinsBears 31-20 over SaintsCowboys 34-24 over TitansChiefs 31-17 over CardinalsSteelers 23-16 over EaglesRavens 20-17 over PanthersBroncos 27-17 over RaidersBYES: Patriots, Browns, Seahawks, Rams, Falcons, Packers

Best pick: Commanders over Giants. Last week, I predicted that the Commanders would score exactly 24 in a win over the Giants, and guess what happened? The Commanders scored exactly 24 points in a win over the Giants. As soon as Sam Hartman got picked to be the next bachelor, I knew there was no way the Commanders were going to lose. Washington decided to distract the Giants by posting thirst traps of Hartman on social media and it clearly worked.

The next Bachelor 🌹#BachelorNation x #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/xjcyF6Ys6q

Hartman is going to go down as the greatest practice squad signing in NFL history.

Worst pick: Texans over Browns. At the rate things are going, I might have to eliminate the "worst pick" section because I'm not getting any picks wrong. Over the past two weeks, I've gone 25-4 straight-up. The hilarious part is that I'm 0-2 when it comes to picking Browns' games and 25-2 in all other games. I think what I'm trying to say here is that I might have to take a week off from picking Browns games, so there will be no Browns pick this week.

Finally, if you guys have ever wondered which teams I'm actually good at picking, I'm going to start sharing that information every week from now through the end of the season. Here's a quick look at my best and worst teams when it comes to picks this year.

Team: I'm 9-1 picking this year (Straight up): Patriots, Eagles (8-1), Jaguars (8-1), Dolphins (8-1), Commanders (7-1-1)My worst teams this year (Straight up): Browns (3-7), Bears (3-6), Buccaneers (3-6)

Every other team is somewhere in the middle.

#2566. How can Warriors survive Stephen Curry's absence? Yaxel Lendeborg has to step up, but that's not all

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Golden State Warriors were riding high with an eight-game winning streak, a breakout rookie in Yaxel Lendeborg and Stephen Curry in MVP form heading into Wednesday's game vs. the Rockets. Then the record cut out at their party when Curry suffered an oblique tear that will cost him at least two weeks and maybe more.

If it is really just a two-week absence, he'll only miss six games and the Warriors will have dodged a bullet. But even that long without Curry is going to be an uphill battle for a team that, its hot start notwithstanding, already has little margin for error.

In general, there are obvious things that need to happen whenever a team loses the superstar that can cover for their mistakes: Limit turnovers (always a problem for the Warriors) and control the glass (Golden State is a relatively good rebounding team and should be able to be even better with some bigger non-Curry lineups; offensive boards go a long way for a team that is now likely to struggle to score for stretches). Winning the possession game will be vital.

You just have to be sharper in general without the ultimate bailout player on the floor. But more specifically, here are three things that probably need to happen for the Warriors to stay afloat without Curry.

After the Houston loss, Draymond Green had this to say about Lendeborg's 25-point, 10-rebound showing that helped fuel a post-Steph-injury surge and kept the Warriors in the game most of the way.

"The thing he's gonna have to learn to understand is, alright, Steph wasn't out there. [Durant] was off the court [for the Rockets]. You look around, you're probably the best player on the floor. Regardless of team. I think there was a point where he realized like, 'Oh, ding ding ding.' And he started attacking, and the game flipped for us.

"I think that's something he's going to have to realize really fast, is like, there will be often times where he could possibly be the best player on the floor regardless of the team. And we need him to show that, and he doesn't have a problem doing it."

This will never be truer than over these next couple of weeks. Lendeborg, a 24-year-old rookie, is now the Warriors' best player, and they need him to play like it. They need aggression. They need the production, from his iso scoring to creation for others to fueling and finishing as many transition attacks as possible.

He's capable of carrying a team. We saw it against the Clippers, when he went for 37 points and six assists with six 3-pointers and just one turnover as the go-to guy with Curry out.

But that was against one of the worst teams in the league (he gets Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs on Friday), and it was a one-night thing when maybe everyone wasn't quite aware of how good he really is. The secret is out now, and Lendeborg's name is going to be the one circled on every opponent's whiteboard moving forward. He'll get the overarching defensive focus. He'll get the double teams. And he'll have the burden of producing big numbers through all that.

There's no question that Lendeborg has looked incredible to start the year. He has the game and confidence to be a No. 1 option even just three weeks into his professional career. He's the Rookie of the Year favorite for a reason, and there has been justified talk about his being a real All-Star candidate. It's too early to be making statements like that, but for as long as Curry is out, Yaxel indeed needs to perform at that kind of level for an offense that doesn't really have anyone else capable of creating consistent advantages.

So far, the Warriors are making 16.5 3-pointers per game at a 39.7% clip. Both of those marks lead the league. A lot of this is Curry, who is making 4.3 triples per game at a truly absurd 45.7% rate given his shot difficulty, but it's not all him.

Give Brandin Podziemski the courtesy of rounding up three-tenths of a percent, and the Warriors have three guys currently making at least two 3s per game with at least a 40% conversion rate.

These are going to be the main gunners, but Golden State has other capable shooters. Georges Niang and Al Horford. LJ Cryer is about to see more time, and he's a 41.7% shooter. Will Richard is at 45.8%. These are all low-volume shooters who now have the green light.

This is how the Warriors stayed competitive against the Rockets: by jacking up 51 3s. They only made 17 of them, but that was still four more than the Rockets. That's a 12-point surplus, and the Warriors can still make plenty of mathematical hay with Curry out.

It won't be easy. His gravity creates a lot of these open looks guys enjoy, and that's where Lendeborg's ability to draw multiple defenders is going to be essential, but if everyone can combine to make just a few more 3s than normal, it can go a long way toward at least partially replacing Curry's 4.3 3s per game in the aggregate.

The Warriors are a top-10 defense (No. 9 if you remove garbage time, per Cleaning the Glass), and though they are giving up almost seven more points per 100 possessions with Curry off the floor, there's some deception in that stat.

Curry is a solid team defender and still better individually than a lot of people think, which is to say he's not going to be the reason your defense is bad. But he's also not the reason this Warriors defense is -- or at least has been -- good, and theoretically they should be just fine without him on that side of the ball. There's even a chance they get better.

De'Anthony Melton will likely start in his place. The Warriors, as mentioned, can play bigger. Curry's juice is infectious and that factors into defensive energy, and the upcoming schedule is a test (San Antonio, Boston and Memphis all register as top-eight offenses), but Green and company know the onus is on the defense to keep Golden State from taking on water without its captain. Are the Warriors up to the challenge?

#2564. Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez named unanimous American League MVP after nearly winning 2026 Triple Crown

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has won the 2026 American League MVP, the BBWAA announced Thursday night.

The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing AL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

Alvarez, 29, bounced back from an injury-riddled disaster in 2025, during which he only played in 48 games. This time around, he avoided the IL and appeared in 158 games. He hit .316/.432/.601 (190 OPS+) with 34 doubles, a triple, 42 home runs, 106 RBI, 105 runs and 6.8 WAR. He made a late run at the Triple Crown, missing out by one home run and seven RBI. He did lead the majors in all three triple slash categories, though, leading in average by five points, on-base percentage by a whopping 42 points -- he led the majors in walks -- and 31 points in slugging percentage. Add the latter two and his OPS victory was 90 points -- 1.033 to second place's .943 (National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong).

The only players in MLB history to lead the majors in all three triple slash categories:

Alvarez becomes just the third Astros player to win MVP after Jeff Bagwell in 1994 and Jose Altuve in 2017.

Rays third baseman Junior Caminero finished in second. At age 22, he played all 162 games, leading the Rays to the best AL record. He hit .276/.360/.524 (144 OPS+) with 42 home runs, 101 RBI and 100 runs, posting a 5.7 WAR. He's already made history, too, as the Rays had previously never had a player finish in the top five of MVP voting.

Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. came in third. This is now his fourth straight season in the top seven and third straight season in the top four. He finished second in 2024. This season, he hit .281/.359/.441 (125 OPS+) with 33 doubles, 18 homers, 54 RBI, 94 runs, 45 steals and 6.7 WAR.

#2563. Six lessons learned from Week 10: Brock Purdy belongs in MVP race, John Harbaugh makes more poor decisions

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

And on the 65th day of the NFL season, everyone finally had a win. The Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens wasn't the prettiest football, but the Chargers will find it as beautiful as any. A long flight home after a win feels a little shorter, and in a season that can't end soon enough, Jim Harbaugh and co., at least for one day, have something to smile about.

Also smiling? The Browns, who watched all of their closest competitors for the final AFC wild card berth fall by the wayside. The only teams within two games -- the Patriots, Raiders and Ravens -- all lost in Week 10 while playing a quarterback who wasn't the Week 1 starter. Add in that the Browns got a crucial win over the Texans, and the AFC playoff picture looks pretty clear.

Over in the NFC, there's a brutal battle. There are nine teams with winning records. The 6-4 Packers hold the No. 7 seed right now, but after a blowout loss to the Vikings, Green Bay finds the Seahawks and Rams -- also 6-4 -- right there. Lots can and will change, but the next time we see the Rams and the Packers facing off on Thanksgiving Eve, it will be arguably the most important game of the year to date.

As the NFC playoff hopefuls scratch and claw, though, they're all looking up at one team, led by one very, very good quarterback.

So much of Brock Purdy's success gets dismissed as him being a cog in the Kyle Shanahan system. And maybe there were times, earlier in his career, when that was closer to the truth.

It is no longer remotely close to the truth. Yes, Shanahan set up some easy release valves for Purdy in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys, like getting Christian McCaffrey matched up against Von Miller for the game-winning touchdown (I wrote about Shanahan deserving Coach of the Year on Sunday), but Purdy was truly magnificent. And he has been pretty much all year.

One play exemplifying this was McCaffrey's first touchdown, when Purdy bought time and, at the last second, found McCaffrey. McCaffrey had been blocking in pass protection just a moment earlier.

BROCK TO CMC OH MYSFvsDAL on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JoKDvzWC3K

The quick feet in the pocket. The full-sprint escape. The pump fake. The stop. The vision. The throw. This is elite quarterbacking.

Purdy had several impressive plays like this one, including a 23-yard completion to Keenan Allen on third-and-12 after getting turned around 180 degrees while escaping a sack. This is what has separated Purdy from previous Shanahan quarterbacks: the creativity and out-of-structure playmaking. Purdy's 0.15 EPA per dropback on throws that take 3.5 seconds or more to come out is second, only to Joe Burrow.

Speaking of Burrow, Purdy won't win MVP, it seems, because Burrow is on a historic heater. He's now a -115 favorite, per DraftKings. Josh Allen is second at +350, followed by Purdy at +425.

But what Purdy, who has never finished above fourth in MVP voting, is doing with an ever-changing carousel of wide receivers is MVP-level stuff. The film matches the numbers, too.

Next up? The Vikings -- a huge chance for Purdy to boost his MVP stock. Speaking of Minnesota ...

We're not just talking about "it looks better," which it absolutely does. We're talking about how Kirk Cousins changes how it looks, as in simply watching the unit moves before the action even happens.

This is why Minnesota got Cousins in the first place. He does everything Kevin O'Connell wants. He's happy to go under center, hit his back foot and let it rip. He doesn't quite rip it as hard as he once did, but the comfort in the system is evident. In fact, one of his most impressive snaps was him getting through audibles to set up a successful screen pass on third and 12.

Excellent work from Kirk Cousins pre-snap.All game, the Vikings were trying to take advantage of the numbers game with screen passes. They got a 4x2 advantage, and pulled the OL to keep the numbers on the outside pic.twitter.com/rXVHc17XDh

Remember, this is five days after he was traded!

The Vikings look very different with Cousins, but Cousins looks very different from the last time he was with the Vikings, too. This was the same field on which he tore his Achilles in 2023, when he was playing some of the best football of his career. He had a rough two seasons in Atlanta and a resurgent half-season in Las Vegas. His movement (he even had two scrambles!) looks so much better than it did in 2024 and 2025. Hearing him after the game was a really cool moment, proving that he not only looks at home, but is, in a broader sense, home.

An emotional Kirk Cousins, in his return to the Vikings at Lambeau Field: “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years…” pic.twitter.com/8PhbEVs7Oq

The Bengals have long had great wide receivers in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and we know how good a healthy Burrow is. But after Sunday night's dismantling of the Steelers, we need to talk about how good this offensive line is, too.

Cincinnati's offensive line stonewalled what's supposed to be a strong Pittsburgh pass rush. Burrow was pressured on just 20.5% of his dropbacks, his lowest rate in over two years. T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith combined for 63 pass-rush snaps ... and ZERO pressures. It's the first time ever both players have been shut out in the same game.

It's a distant memory now, but the Bengals came into this year wanting to do more under-center stuff to help the run game and the offensive line. But the running game hasn't materialized, and the offensive line simply doesn't need the help of under-center and/or play-action concepts.

The Bengals are fifth in PFF's pass-blocking grade this year. They were 26th last year and 29th the year before that. What a huge jump, and in a great year to have one, too.

Going back to where the week started. The Giants bungled a chance to get closer to putting this division away. Yes, give the Commanders credit where credit is due, but John Harbaugh was a huge part of New York's collapse.

There are two conservative choices Harbaugh made late in the fourth quarter that stand out. The first was fourth-and-1 at the Giants' own 11-yard line with 3:26 left.

Yes, their OWN 11-yard line. And, yes, they should've gone for it. This is reminiscent of the Lions going for it in nearly the exact same scenario in Week 7, which I wrote about back then. As Dan Campbell explained, he 1) thought his team would convert and 2) knew if it didn't, it would almost certainly get the ball back with a decent chunk of time left. The Lions failed, but Green Bay missed a kick, and the Lions ran the clock out.

The same applied here, and Jameis Winston has been really good at quarterback sneaks, too, the previous play notwithstanding.

Instead, Winston barked out his now-infamous "Who let the dogs out?" cadence, and the Giants took a delay-of-game penalty and punted. According to Ben Baldwin's fourth-down decision bot, 101 out of 101 models favored the Giants going for it.

If you listen to nothing else today, at least listen to Jameis Winston's hard count here lmao 😂 pic.twitter.com/F1nr26EN3W

After a Jayden Daniels interception, the Giants again played it safe with three straight runs, including a designed J.J. McCarthy run on third and 3. Sonny Styles sniffed it out for a 2-yard loss; the Commanders had been all over McCarthy's designed runs. Models were split on the fourth-and-5 decision; the Giants punted again, and to make matters worse, Jordan Stout shanked the punt 12 yards. Daniels led the game-winning touchdown drive, and Washington now has life.

Overall, Harbaugh's conservative decisions -- he had another one in the fourth quarter and one in the first quarter, too -- cost New York about 11.4% win probability, per Baldwin's bot. That's rough. If New York doesn't make the postseason, Winton's silly cadence will re-emerge for all the wrong reasons.

Fernando Mendoza's first career was the top headline for what ended up being a 21-13 Raiders loss to the Seahawks, but Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald, special teams coordinator Jay Harbaugh and wide receiver Tory Horton teamed up for one of the smartest plays you'll see.

The effort by the Seahawks special teams to prevent the touchback and keep the clock running 👏SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YF6eTRh4gs

'"Nine yards, 11 inches (into the end zone) -- literally, if there's any way to return the ball, return the ball,'" Harbaugh told his kickoff-return team. 'Burning the two-minute (warning on the kickoff return) is so impactful at that time.'"

Harbaugh even reminded his unit of that right before it went onto the field, and then Horton defied gravity to do exactly what Harbaugh had asked.

I love how Macdonald celebrated with Horton. The term "player's coach" is overrated and overused, but Macdonald clearly gets it. So, too does his staff and his team. And for those wondering about "illegal batting," it would have been a 10-yard penalty and a re-kick, which would have occurred within two minutes. Las Vegas obviously declined.

We've seen so many clock mismanagements, especially on special teams, this season. Getting little details like this right is a sign of a coaching staff and team that's 100% bought in. We'd expect nothing less from the reigning champs.

There have been 21 games decided by 15+ points over the past three weeks. In the seven weeks before that, there were only 26.

We're starting to see the effects of the massive wave of quarterback injuries. The Patriots and Jets both lost their starters during Week 10, and the Cardinals are now on their third quarterback of the year. They accounted for three of the seven losses by 15+ this week. (Steelers, Titans, Packers and Falcons, you have no excuses).

This might be the way it is going forward, too. The Colts and the Dolphins played one another in Week 10, but they project as two of the league's worst teams, and they play the Texans and the Bills, respectively, in Week 11. The Cardinals face the Chiefs. Unfortunately, there are just a lot of teams playing out the string already.

#2562. Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong wins National League MVP unanimously, beating Shohei Ohtani

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the National League MVP award for the 2026 season unanimously, the BBWAA revealed Thursday evening.

The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing NL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

Though the results were unsurprising by the time the year wound down, going back to the start of the season, this marks a huge upset. Shohei Ohtani was the overwhelming favorite to win the award heading into the season and maintained favorite status through the All-Star break. A combination of his injuries and PCA's monster season turned the tide late.

Appearing in all 162 games, Crow-Armstrong hit .280/.372/.570 (156 OPS+) with 31 doubles, eight triples, 45 home runs, 107 RBI, 119 runs, 41 steals and 9.8 WAR. He led the majors in WAR, runs, home runs and total bases while leading the NL in slugging, OPS and OPS+. He became the seventh player in MLB history to join the 40-40 club (40 home runs and 40 steals in the same season). Further, he led the majors in multiple advanced defensive metrics, putting together one of the great all-around seasons from a position player in recent memory.

PCA joins the following list of Cubs to win MVP:

Ohtani, the four-time MVP, finishes in second. At the plate, Ohtani hit .275/.377/.512 with 26 doubles, four triples, 30 home runs, 81 RBI, 89 runs, 11 steals and 3.2 WAR. On the mound, he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 95 strikeouts in 85 ⅔ innings with 3.2 WAR.

The nationally underrated Brewers second baseman Brice Turang finishes in third. He still hasn't made an All-Star Game, though he did start 2026 as a member of Team USA in the World Baseball Classic. In the regular season, Turang hit .268/.366/.450 (124 OPS+) with 37 doubles, three triples, 21 home runs, 100 RBI, 102 runs and 7.3 WAR, rating out as one of the best defenders in baseball.
